growth_010:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare launch assets and copy for our Product Hunt and startup directory launch. If you don't already have them, ask me for: our product name, domain, one-line tagline, longer description (2-3 sentences), target audience, 3-5 key features/benefits, any existing logo/screenshots/demo video links, our maker/founder name and title, and links to our Twitter/X, LinkedIn, and any relevant communities. 

Once you have these, produce: (1) A Product Hunt listing draft: tagline (under 60 characters), description (under 260 characters), and a longer 'first comment' maker note explaining why we built this and what's new. (2) A checklist of required visual assets per Product Hunt's guidelines (gallery images, thumbnail/logo sizes, optional demo GIF or video) noting which we already have and which still need to be created. (3) Three short copy variants (1-2 sentences each) suitable for submitting to general startup directories, adapted in tone/length as needed. (4) A short outreach message template I can send to my network (email and social post versions) asking for support on launch day, without making false urgency claims. 

Write everything in a single organized document (or reply inline if no doc tool is available), clearly labeled by section. Do not submit anything to Product Hunt or any directory yet — this step is only asset and copy preparation. When finished, report back a summary of what you drafted, a list of any assets or information still missing from me, and flag anything that needs my review before submission.

growth_010:n2.prompt:
You are helping me submit our product to Product Hunt as part of our launch-day plan. If you don't already have these from me, ask for: (1) my domain/product URL, (2) product name and a short tagline (under 60 characters), (3) a 2-3 sentence description of what the product does and who it's for, (4) any launch-day promo details (discount code, offer), (5) a first maker comment draft, and (6) links to prepared visual assets (logo, gallery images/screenshots, optional demo video/GIF) — ask where these files are stored if not provided.

Then do the following:
1. Using your configured credentials, log into Product Hunt.
2. Start a new product submission (maker submission form).
3. Fill in the product name, tagline, and description using the copy I gave you, refining wording only for clarity and character limits — flag any changes back to me.
4. Upload the logo and gallery images/video in the correct required formats and dimensions per the form's guidance.
5. Add the product URL, relevant topic/category tags, and the maker comment draft in the appropriate field.
6. Set or confirm the launch date/time if the form allows scheduling.
7. Review the full submission preview for typos, broken links, or missing assets.

Once everything is filled in and reviewed, stop for human sign-off before hitting submit or publish — do not submit the listing yourself.

Report back with: a summary of every field you filled in and its final content, confirmation of which assets uploaded successfully (and any that failed), the scheduled launch date/time if set, and a direct link to the draft/preview so I can do a final check and submit it myself.

growth_010:n3.prompt:
You are helping me submit my startup to a set of startup directories as part of my Product Hunt launch-day push. Before starting, ask me for anything missing: my company name, one-line tagline, short description (2-4 sentences), website URL, logo image file or link, category/tags, my Product Hunt launch URL, and any preferred contact email to use on submissions.

Goal: submit our listing to as many relevant startup directories as possible using standard web submission forms, so each listing is live or pending review by end of launch day.

Actions:
1. Compile a target list of well-known startup directories that accept public submissions (e.g., BetaList, Launching Next, StartupBase, SaaSHub, AlternativeTo, Indie Hackers, There's An AI For That if relevant, Crunchbase, AngelList/Wellfound company profile, G2, Capterra — adjust based on relevance to my product).
2. For each directory, locate its submission form, fill in the required fields using the details I provided (name, tagline, description, URL, logo, category), and submit using my configured credentials where a login is required.
3. Keep a running log noting: directory name, submission URL, status (submitted/pending/live), and any confirmation email or ticket ID received.
4. Flag any directory that requires payment, a phone call, manual editorial review, or unusual verification steps — skip those and note them separately rather than attempting workarounds.

Done looks like: submissions completed on all directories that have a straightforward self-serve form, with confirmation of receipt where the platform provides one.

Report back: a table listing each directory, submission status, confirmation reference (if any), and a short list of directories skipped along with the reason (e.g., paid tier, manual review only).

growth_010:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare launch-day outreach materials to rally my network for our Product Hunt launch, since the actual personal asking (calls/texts/DMs to specific people) remains a human step that only I can do.

First, ask me for: (1) my Product Hunt listing URL (or confirm it isn't live yet), (2) my company/product name and one-line pitch, (3) a rough list or categories of people I want to rally (e.g., close friends, investors, past customers, Slack/Discord communities, Twitter/X followers, LinkedIn connections), and (4) my launch date/time and timezone.

Once I provide these, please draft ready-to-send outreach copy tailored to each audience segment, including:
- A short, casual text/DM message for close friends and family asking them to upvote and comment on Product Hunt.
- A slightly more formal message for investors/advisors, framing the ask around supporting the launch.
- A social post draft for Twitter/X and LinkedIn announcing the launch and asking for support, with placeholder space for the live Product Hunt link.
- A message template for relevant Slack/Discord communities or group chats, respecting each community's self-promotion norms.
- A simple checklist of who to contact, in what order, and via which channel (text, email, DM, group post), based on the audience list I gave you.

Organize all drafts and the checklist into a single document or message so I can quickly copy-paste and personalize each one on launch morning.

When the drafts and checklist are ready, report back with the full text of each message variant and the outreach checklist, then stop for human sign-off — do not send any messages, post on my behalf, or contact anyone directly, since rallying my network is a personal, relationship-driven action I need to execute myself.

growth_010:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track the signup spike from our Product Hunt / directory launch using {{vendor}}, our product-analytics tool. If any of the following are missing, ask me for them first: (1) the domain or app where signups happen, (2) our {{vendor}} project/workspace identifier and confirmation that you can use my already-configured credentials, (3) the exact launch date and time window (including timezone) to analyze, and (4) how a 'signup' event is defined in our tracking (event name or conversion goal).

Once you have these, use the {{vendor}} query API (or MCP server if available) to: 1) pull signup counts broken down by hour (or the smallest available granularity) for the launch day and the 3-7 days immediately prior as a baseline; 2) calculate the percentage increase in signups on launch day versus the average of the baseline period; 3) identify the peak hour of signups and correlate it with when we posted/promoted the launch, if timestamps are available; 4) if raw event export is available and useful, pull a sample of raw signup events during the peak window to check for data quality issues (duplicates, bot traffic, etc.).

Done looks like: a concise report showing (a) total launch-day signups vs baseline average, (b) percentage spike, (c) peak hour and its magnitude, (d) any data quality flags, and (e) a simple hour-by-hour or day-by-day chart/table of signup counts for the tracked window.

Report back with this summary in plain text or markdown, including the raw numbers you pulled and the exact date range and event definition used, so I can sanity-check the analysis.
